lines.text: Paul begins his defense before King Agrippa and says he lived as a Pharisee, the strictest sect of their religion.
With authority from the chief priests, Paul imprisoned many saints and was on his way to Antioch to persecute more.
About noon on the road, a light brighter than the sun shone, and Jesus appointed Paul as a servant and witness.
The Jews seized Paul in the synagogues and tried to kill him, though he had God's help to this day.
Agrippa told Festus that Paul could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.
